article.title: Trump lost Congress. The US is losing the world | w/ Vijay Prashad
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: Iran is still restricting the Strait of Hormuz, Ukraine’s front lines haven’t moved, and China won’t be contained. Even before voters handed Democrats Congress, Vijay Prashad argues Washington was already losing its grip on the world. The Tricontinental executive director joins Rania Khalek and Zoe Alexandra from Kenya to break down what the 2026 midterms mean for US foreign policy. As Trump admits the Iran war cost Republicans, and JD Vance blames it outright, Prashad says the US is “at a loss strategically,” with Tehran holding the leverage, backed by Russia and China. Prashad is hopeful that new faces like Abdul El-Sayed and six new DSA members, backed by pressure from below, can force “irrelevant” Schumer and Jeffries to answer to the new progressive wing. Khalek pushes back: insurgents will be co-opted, zionist corporate-backed Dems still hold the power, and the fight over leadership matters. They also discuss Palestinian parties holding the balance of power in Israel’s Knesset, Europe’s backlash against militarization and conscription, why Prashad thinks a Democratic Congress is too late to change the war in Ukraine or the drive to war with China, and why Lula’s re-election in Brazil shows Trump “lost the hemisphere.” Watch full episodes of BT Live, join breakthroughnews.org as a member today! #breakthroughnews ****** Rough transcript follows: [Interviewer:] Welcome to the show, Vijay Prashad, Executive Director of the Tricontinental Institute for Social Research. [Vijay Prashad:] Thanks for having me. It’s an honor to be your first guest. [Interviewer:] We’re excited to have you. Let’s start with the unpopular war in Iran. We’ve heard from JD Vance, Trump, and polling that indicates people in the US voted against the Iran war. However, Iran doesn’t see this as a change of heart. Khamenei said expecting partisan change to end US hostility is gravely mistaken. Can Trump still prosecute this war after losing Congress? Do his prospects change with a Democrat-controlled Congress, and do they want to end this war? [Vijay Prashad:] Firstly, I was talking to people in Tehran, and they joked that Trump and Netanyahu started a war thinking they’d change the regime in Tehran, but instead, it created regime change in Israel and Washington. Interestingly, on November 2nd, before the election, IRGC head Mohsen Rezaei had a 90-minute phone call with Vladimir Putin. On November 5th, Rezaei flew to Moscow with a message from Ayatollah Khamenei. Russia and China have been in talks, wanting to see hostilities decrease. The US attack on Qeshm Island was minimal, and the US is not strategically capable of further attacks on Iran. Iran holds the cards and demands confidence-building measures, such as ending the embargo on the Strait of Hormuz and releasing frozen assets. The US is at a loss on how to proceed. Democrats coming into Washington, with the increase of Democratic Socialists of America, might bring new voices. If they are more like Rashida Tlaib than Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, they could be interesting voices. Even though it’s the party of Biden, the new representatives might propose legislation to prevent more war and suffering. [Interviewer:] It’s exciting to have people who speak against sanctions and bombing campaigns. However, the Democratic Party was responsible for the initial genocide in Gaza. There hasn’t been accountability, and the leadership remains Zionist and imperialist. Do you see a change in Israel policy, or will it be the same policies glossed over with liberalism? [Vijay Prashad:] Politics doesn’t happen in a straight line. In Israel, a historic number of Palestinians voted, resulting in a high number of Palestinian lawmakers in the Knesset. They now hold the keys, demanding a rollback of apartheid policies. In the US, pressure from below is crucial. Newly elected representatives need to be informed about the implications of foreign policy on domestic issues. The new class should challenge Schumer and Jeffries’ leadership. [Interviewer:] While it’s important to be optimistic, we must remember recent history. Some insurgent candidates might compromise once in power. The Democratic Party is still run by corporate interests, and movement building outside the party remains crucial. [Vijay Prashad:] I agree, but it’s also okay to declare victory. Trump’s defeat is significant, and millions voted against his policies. The focus should be on organizing their thinking and putting pressure on newly elected officials. This wasn’t a victory for Schumer and Jeffries; it’s about the people who voted against Trump’s policies. [Interviewer:] Let’s discuss the war in Ukraine. Democrats support funding the war, and some progressive insurgents are on board. What does a Democratic Congress mean for NATO, and how long will this war continue? [Vijay Prashad:] The new Congress is late to the game. Europe is on fire, with people protesting military spending. No one wants to die in a Ukrainian ditch. The war is over, and the only solution is a conclusive peace settlement. More money to Ukraine won’t change the situation. [Interviewer:] Regarding China, do Democrats represent a break in the drive to war, or will they try to outflank Trump as hawks on China? [Vijay Prashad:] It’s too late. The US establishment acknowledges it’s too late to push China’s development back. China’s economic advancement is the real threat, not military. The US can’t intimidate China, and it must focus on building its own infrastructure. The world is no longer willing to be intimidated. [Interviewer:] Thank you, Vijay Prashad, for joining us. We look forward to discussing more topics with you in the future.
